title: Nausea and Vomiting
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset fever, hypotension, diffuse erythematous rash (sunburn-like with desquamation 1-2 weeks later), and multisystem involvement (GI: nausea/vomiting/diarrhea, renal, hepatic, CNS, hematologic). Caused by TSST-1 superantigen from S. aureus (menstrual — tampon use) or Group A Strep. TSS diagnosis: fever + hypotension + rash + ≥3 organ systems. Remove source (tampon, wound packing). Blood cultures, wound cultures. Treatment: aggressive IV fluids, vasopressors if needed, empiric IV antibiotics (vancomycin + clindamycin — clindamycin suppresses toxin production). IVIG may be considered in severe cases. Admit to ICU.
